## GitHub code scanning[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/github-code-scanning.html#github-code-scanning)

The `sarif` format feeds GitHub code scanning on the GitHub mirror. This page adds the workflow that uploads the log with the official action, pinned to a full commit SHA. Run the check with `--format=sarif`, and let the scanner show the findings on the files. PROCTOR now files the mark sheet in the format the head office already reads; no more translating the exam results by hand.

### The workflow[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/github-code-scanning.html#the-workflow)

Add this workflow to the mirror. It sets up PHP, installs PROCTOR, runs the check against the app's CREED policy file, and uploads the resulting log:

```yaml
name: proctor
on: [push, pull_request]
permissions:
  security-events: write
jobs:
  proctor:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: shivammathur/setup-php@v2
        with:
          php-version: '8.4'
      - run: composer require waynestate/proctor --dev
      # policy.json is the CREED policy file
      - run: vendor/bin/proctor check --format=sarif --policy=policy.json > proctor.sarif
      - uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@9b3254085494b55a0f7c4c2b3d2d52cc712ce370 # v4.39.1
        with:
          sarif_file: proctor.sarif
```

The `--policy=policy.json` argument names the app's CREED policy file; see [Policy](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/policy.html) for how PROCTOR finds one when you do not name it.

### What the log contains[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/github-code-scanning.html#what-the-log-contains)

The uploaded `proctor.sarif` is a SARIF 2.1.0 log: one run, one rule per check, one result per non-pass finding.

- The driver block names the tool `proctor`, its version, and the repository's information URI.
- The rules list holds one entry per distinct rule id in the report, in first-seen order, each with a short description carrying the id.
- Each result holds `ruleId`, `level`, `message.text` and one location. The level maps `fail` to `error`, `warning` to `warning`, and any other non-pass status to `note`.
- The location uses the finding's path (backslashes normalized to forward slashes) and its line as `region.startLine`; a finding without a path points at the app's `composer.json`.
- Each result also carries `partialFingerprints` with the finding's fingerprint under `proctorFingerprint/v1`, the stable identity of the finding.

See [Formats](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/formats.html) for the shape of every format.

### Related[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/github-code-scanning.html#related)

- [Formats](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/formats.html)
- [Policy](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/policy.html)
- [CI checks](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/check-ci.html)
- [Rule ids](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/rule-ids.html)

## Overrides[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/overrides.html#overrides)

This page explains how an app carries a `policy-overrides.json` file next to its composer.json to waive a check's fail findings until an expiry date. Add an entry for a temporary exception, keep it dated, and remove it before it expires. An approval, like an exam excuse, needs a date.

### How overrides work[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/overrides.html#how-overrides-work)

- An expired override fails the `overrides` check.
- An active override turns the check's fail findings into warnings.
- An override has a maximum duration: an entry whose expiry lies more than `rules.override_max_days` days after `--today` (90 days when the key is absent) fails the `overrides` check (`proctor/overrides/too-long`) and is not applied. The cap exists because an approval is a dated exception, not a standing one, and CREED allows no permanent override.
- An override never waives a failure whose state is EOL plus grace (`eol_grace_expired`); that failure stands (the stack's version policy decision).
- PROCTOR rejects the file (exit 2) when an entry names a check that is not registered in the run, or names the `overrides` check itself: an override cannot exempt the check that polices overrides, and an entry for a check that does not exist would silently do nothing.
- The list of valid check ids is built from the checks PROCTOR runs, so a new check needs no change to the guard.
- An active override that expires within 14 days of `--today` (the expiry day counts) gets a warning finding (`proctor/overrides/expiring`) instead of lapsing without a trace, and an active override whose check raised no failure gets a warning finding (`proctor/overrides/unused`) so a stale approval is removed instead of rotting.
- A warning never changes the exit code.
- In `proctor gate`, an expired override blocks the deploy whatever the baseline says, even when its check is not one the gate runs (see [Deploy gate](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/deploy-gate.html)).
- When the app has no `policy-overrides.json`, the check produces no findings at all: it passes and prints nothing. Every override, active or expired, is printed as an OVERRIDE line by the CLI in addition to these findings.

Warning

An expired override fails the run. Renew it or delete it before the expiry date.

### When the audit cannot run[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/overrides.html#when-the-audit-cannot-run)

`composer-audit` fails (`proctor/composer-audit/skipped`) with a message that starts with `not audited:` in two cases: the composer executable is not on PATH, and the app path has no composer.lock. Until Composer is installed or the lock is committed, an active `composer-audit` entry downgrades those fails to warnings:

```json
[
    {
        "check": "composer-audit",
        "reason": "no lock yet, ticket in progress",
        "expires": "2026-12-01",
        "approved_by": "tester"
    }
]
```

An entry needs a `check`, a `reason`, an `expires` date and an `approved_by`; a file missing any of them is rejected (exit 2). Remove the entry when the audit can run again, so the approval does not rot.

### Backing an audit ignore entry[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/overrides.html#backing-an-audit-ignore-entry)

`composer-audit` fails each ignore entry in composer.json that no active `composer-audit` override backs (`proctor/composer-audit/unbacked-ignore`), because an ignore without a dated approval never expires. An override backs the entry when its `advisory` field equals the entry's advisory id case-insensitively, its `package` field matches the entry's package the way composer matches patterns, or it carries no scope at all; an entry that names neither an id nor a package (an ignore-severity level) is backed by an unscoped override only. An override that backs an entry is not reported unused. To back an `ignore-id` entry for CVE-2024-52301:

```json
[
    {
        "check": "composer-audit",
        "advisory": "CVE-2024-52301",
        "reason": "patch lands with the next framework release",
        "expires": "2026-12-01",
        "approved_by": "tester"
    }
]
```

Remove the ignore entry from composer.json when the override expires, so the approval and the silence end on the same date.

### Verify the date window[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/overrides.html#verify-the-date-window)

Use `--today=YYYY-MM-DD` to make the 14-day warning window deterministic. For example, an entry that expires on the same day as `--today` is still inside the window, because the expiry day counts. The same flag makes the maximum-duration boundary deterministic: an entry whose expiry lies exactly `override_max_days` days after `--today` still applies, and one day more fails with `proctor/overrides/too-long`.

Run the check against the app path:

```bash
vendor/bin/proctor check --path=. --today=YYYY-MM-DD
```

### Rule ids[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/overrides.html#rule-ids)

| Check | Rule id |
| --- | --- |
| `overrides` | `proctor/overrides` |
| `overrides` | `proctor/overrides/expiring` |
| `overrides` | `proctor/overrides/too-long` |
| `overrides` | `proctor/overrides/unused` |

- [CI checks](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/check-ci.html)
- [WayneUI checks](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/check-wayneui.html)

## Policy[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/policy.html#policy)

This page explains which CREED-format policy file PROCTOR checks against, and how to point it at a different one. Pick the source that fits the app (an explicit file, an environment variable, the CREED package, or the bundled copy), then confirm in the report which policy the run actually used. The proctor grades against the school's answer key, not its own memory, and it always says which key it used.

### What a policy file contains[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/policy.html#what-a-policy-file-contains)

`--policy` takes a CREED-format policy file: schema_version 1, component versions with released, active_until and security_until dates, and rules (audit_severity_threshold, abandoned_packages, banned_constraints, eol_grace_days). The policy-file wiring to `waynestate/creed` is described in [The CREED reader copy](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/policy.html#the-creed-reader-copy) below.

### Resolution order[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/policy.html#resolution-order)

PROCTOR resolves the policy in this order, first match wins:

1. The `--policy` option, naming a policy file (origin `option`).
2. The `PROCTOR_POLICY` environment variable, naming a policy file (origin `env`).
3. `<app>/vendor/waynestate/creed/policy/policy.json`, when it exists, is readable, and is at least as fresh as the bundled copy (origin `vendor`).
4. The policy bundled with PROCTOR, `src/Creed/policy.json` (origin `bundled`).

Name the policy explicitly:

```bash
vendor/bin/proctor check --policy=policy.json
```

Or set the environment variable for the shell:

Linux / macOS

```sh
export PROCTOR_POLICY=/path/to/policy.json
vendor/bin/proctor check
```

Windows (PowerShell)

```powershell
$env:PROCTOR_POLICY = 'C:\path\to\policy.json'
vendor/bin/proctor check
```

Note

The resolver reads each candidate's top-level `refreshed_on` date from the raw JSON and treats it as a date only when it is an ISO date (`YYYY-MM-DD`). A value that is absent or not one is treated as absent.

### The vendor copy[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/policy.html#the-vendor-copy)

An app that installs CREED gets its policy automatically:

```bash
composer require waynestate/creed --dev
```

The vendor copy wins over the bundled one only when it is at least as fresh: its `refreshed_on` is the same as or newer than the bundled copy's (ISO dates compare as strings), or the bundled copy has no `refreshed_on` date at all.

A vendor copy that cannot be read or parsed is skipped with a note on stderr and the run continues with the next source; a vendor copy older than the bundled one is skipped the same way. The notes PROCTOR can print:

- `Skipping vendor policy <path>: the file could not be read.`
- `Skipping vendor policy <path>: invalid JSON (<reason>).`
- `Skipping vendor policy <path>: <reason>.` when the CREED reader rejects the file
- `Using the bundled policy: the vendor copy at <path> (refreshed <date>) is older than the bundled copy (refreshed <date>).` When a copy has no date, its slot reads `without a refreshed_on date` instead.

Warning

An explicit source (`--policy` or `PROCTOR_POLICY`) that points at a missing or invalid file is still an error (exit 2). Only the vendor copy is skipped quietly.

### Policy and date in CI[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/policy.html#policy-and-date-in-ci)

In CI (any of `CI`, `GITLAB_CI` or `GITHUB_ACTIONS` set to a value other than `0` or `false`), `--policy` and `--today` are refused with a tool error (exit 2): in CI the policy and the date must come from the stack, not from the app being checked, so a pipeline that could pass its own policy or date in its own `.gitlab-ci.yml` could grade itself. The refusal message names the option or options that were given.

The `PROCTOR_POLICY` environment variable stays allowed in CI; it is how a trusted job names a policy. A trusted job (a protected or group-level CI variable, never the app's own `.gitlab-ci.yml`) can allow the two options by setting `PROCTOR_ALLOW_OVERRIDES` to exactly `1`:

```yaml
# Group Settings > CI/CD > Variables: name PROCTOR_ALLOW_OVERRIDES, value 1,
# type Variable, scope Protected. Never in the app's own .gitlab-ci.yml.
PROCTOR_ALLOW_OVERRIDES: "1"
```

Outside CI nothing changes: both options work as described above.

### What the report says[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/policy.html#what-the-report-says)

Every report names the policy it used: origin (`option`, `env`, `vendor` or `bundled`), path, `refreshed_on` and the age in days. The age is whole days since the refresh: zero on the refresh day, positive after it, negative when the date is in the future, and absent when the policy carries no `refreshed_on`.

The `policy-age` check warns when the policy is more than 60 days old, or when a non-bundled policy has no `refreshed_on` date, so a stopped CREED refresh is visible instead of silent.

### The CREED reader copy[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/policy.html#the-creed-reader-copy)

PROCTOR carries a generated copy of the CREED reader under `src/Creed/` (namespace `Waynestate\Proctor\Creed`), so it never depends on the CREED package at runtime. `composer creed-copy:check` verifies the copy against the CREED checkout named by `CREED_PATH` (default `../creed`); refresh it by running CREED's `bin/export.php` against `src/Creed/`.

Weekly CREED copy refresh: a scheduled GitLab job (`creed-copy-refresh`, Mondays, an hour after CREED's policy robot) re-exports the copy from CREED main, rebuilds the docs, runs `composer creed-copy:check` and `composer ci`, and pushes to main only when both pass. A red run leaves main untouched.

## Quick start[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html#quick-start)

Pencils up. Five minutes, one command, a mark sheet: install PROCTOR, run the first check, read what the proctor saw.

1. Add PROCTOR to the app as a dev dependency.
   ```
   composer require waynestate/proctor --dev
   ```
   Expected: Composer installs it, and the command is then `vendor/bin/proctor`.
2. Run the first check.
   ```
   vendor/bin/proctor check
   ```
   Expected: the text report. A header line with the tool and the composer version, a line naming the policy in use, one line per finding written in words, then a RESULT line. Exit 0 when nothing failed (warnings allowed), 1 when something did.
   ![Nine real lines from PROCTOR's text report, one per check, each written in words](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/report.svg)
3. Read the mark sheet.
   Every finding carries a stable, namespaced rule id: `proctor/<check-id>` for a check's default finding, `proctor/<check-id>/<rule>` for a named rule. A FAIL is a resit; a WARN is a note in the margin; an INFO is the proctor thinking out loud.
4. Make the run deterministic.
   ```
   vendor/bin/proctor check --today=2026-01-01 --php-runtime=8.4.0
   ```
   Expected: the same marks on every run. `--today` overrides today's date so runs are deterministic, and `--php-runtime` tells the `unpatched` check the PHP version that will serve the app. CI should pass the deploy image's PHP, not the runner's.
5. Emit a machine-readable mark sheet (optional).
   ```
   vendor/bin/proctor check --format=json
   ```
   Use `--format=codequality` for GitLab's Code Quality JSON, or `--format=sarif` for a SARIF 2.1.0 log that GitHub code scanning can read.
6. Name the policy explicitly (optional).
   ```
   vendor/bin/proctor check --policy=policy.json
   ```
   Without `--policy`, PROCTOR resolves the policy in this order: the `PROCTOR_POLICY` environment variable, the app's `vendor/waynestate/creed/policy/policy.json`, then the copy bundled with PROCTOR.

### What you built[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html#what-you-built)

You ran PROCTOR's first marking pass: a verdict per check against the CREED policy, with an exit code CI can gate on. Nothing in the app changed; the proctor only watches.

### Next steps[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html#next-steps)

- [Install](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html): requirements and the single-file PHAR route for apps without Composer access.
- [Reference: commands](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html): the long-form docs for the commands, [rule ids](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/rule-ids.html) and [exit codes](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/exit-codes.html).
- When you are ready for CI, the README's GitHub code scanning section shows a workflow that runs the check with `--format=sarif` and uploads the log to code scanning.

Source: https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/

## Overview[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/#overview)

![PROCTOR's front page: a green examination book sealed with PROCTOR's eye mark, beside the headline 'Watches the exam. Doesn't help.'](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/hero.jpg)

PROCTOR: Policy Rules Of Code, Tested On Release. It is the proctor your composer.lock didn't know it needed: a framework-free PHP CLI that measures a PHP application against the WSU version policy. No phones, no EOL PHP. It reads the app's composer.json and composer.lock, decides the support state of the app's PHP floor from a policy file, and reports each check as pass, warning, info or fail. The checks and their rules come from the stack's version policy decision and from the policy file passed with `--policy`; PROCTOR itself holds no policy of its own.

Note

**Not to be confused with:** code style is Pinstripe, CI is Preflight. PROCTOR grades an app against CREED's rules.

### Install and first run[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/#install-and-first-run)

Add PROCTOR to the app as a dev dependency:

```
composer require waynestate/proctor --dev
```

The command is then `vendor/bin/proctor`. Run it against the app:

```
vendor/bin/proctor check [--path=.] [--format=text|json|codequality|sarif] [--policy=<file>] [--today=YYYY-MM-DD] [--php-runtime=X.Y.Z] [--timeout=300]
```

A clean hall exits 0 (warnings allowed), a resit exits 1, and a tripped proctor exits 2.

### Pick your path[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/#pick-your-path)

- [Quick start](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html): install PROCTOR, run the first check and read the mark sheet.
- [Install](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html): requirements, the composer line and the single-file PHAR route.
- [Deploy gate](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/deploy-gate.html): `proctor gate` gives a release script a go or no-go, ratcheted against what is already running.
- Reference: the long-form docs for the [commands](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html), [rule ids](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/rule-ids.html) and [exit codes](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/exit-codes.html).

### Status[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/#status)

Version: Unreleased. License: MIT.

Agents: the machine-readable entry point for this documentation is [llms.txt](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt).

## Install[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#install)

### Requirements[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#requirements)

- PHP `^8.3`. composer.json pins the platform to `8.3.0`, so the package resolves against 8.3 and runs on anything newer.
- No PHP extensions. composer.json declares no `ext-*` requirement; the runtime libraries (`symfony/console`, `symfony/yaml`, `composer/semver`, `nikic/php-parser`) arrive as Composer packages.
- Composer, for the main install path below. The single-file PHAR route needs only a PHP CLI and a download from the GitLab Release.
- GitLab 18.7 or later for the stack's CI (the stack's CI components use `spec:component`). See BEST_PRACTICES 8.7.

Where the code lives: the canonical repository is on git.wayne.edu, [enterprise-apps/proctor](https://git.wayne.edu/enterprise-apps/proctor). GitHub ([waynestate/proctor](https://github.com/waynestate/proctor)) is a read-only mirror of it. Open issues and merge requests on git.wayne.edu, not on the mirror. Your proctor keeps one answer sheet, and this is it; the mirrors hold photocopies.

### Single-file PHAR[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#single-file-phar)

The single-file PHAR is how Preflight and apps without Composer access run PROCTOR as one file, and from the next release it is attached to each GitLab Release with its `proctor.phar.sha256` checksum file. Both files come from the `release-phar` job in `.gitlab-ci.yml`; the lead tags, and no tag means no release. The `composer require` install below stays the current method; the phar is the one-file alternative.

Download both files for the tag you want, verify the checksum, then run it. Replace `<release>` with the base URL of the release's asset links (the release page lists both files).

Linux / macOS (sh), one line:

```sh
curl -fsSL -o proctor.phar "<release>/proctor.phar" -o proctor.phar.sha256 "<release>/proctor.phar.sha256" && sha256sum -c proctor.phar.sha256 && php proctor.phar --version
```

Windows (PowerShell), one line, no bash needed:

```powershell
Invoke-WebRequest "<release>/proctor.phar" -OutFile proctor.phar; Invoke-WebRequest "<release>/proctor.phar.sha256" -OutFile proctor.phar.sha256; if ((Get-FileHash proctor.phar -Algorithm SHA256).Hash -ne (Get-Content proctor.phar.sha256 -TotalCount 1).Trim().Split(' ')[0]) { throw "sha256 mismatch" }; php proctor.phar --version
```

Until the first tagged release that runs the job, build it from a checkout with the script for your OS (both need Docker, and no PHP or Composer on the host): `.\scripts\build-phar.ps1` on Windows, `scripts/build-phar.sh` on Linux / macOS. Each script writes `build/proctor.phar` and verifies it by printing PROCTOR's version.

### Install[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#install-1)

```
composer require waynestate/proctor --dev
```

The command is then `vendor/bin/proctor`.

### Verify[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#verify)

Run the check against the app:

```
vendor/bin/proctor check
```

Expected: the text report. A header line with the tool and the versions of the external tools used (composer), a line naming the policy in use (origin, path, refresh date), one line per finding, one line per override, then a RESULT line. Exit codes: 0 for pass (warnings allowed), 1 for one or more failures, 2 for a tool error. A proctor that prints a mark sheet is a proctor that is on duty.

### Next steps[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#next-steps)

- [Quick start](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html): run the first check and read the report.
- [Reference: commands](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html): every command and option, with the [rule ids](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/rule-ids.html) and [exit codes](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/exit-codes.html) alongside.

## Commands[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#commands)

Every command PROCTOR ships, with the options each one accepts. The table is generated from the CLI, so it stays in step with the code; a proctor reads the rules aloud before the exam, it does not take the exam for you. If you have not run a check yet, start with the [Quick start](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html).

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `proctor check` | Measure a PHP app against the version policy. |
| `proctor gate` | Decide go or no-go for a deploy: the deploy-time checks, ratcheted against a baseline. |

#### `proctor check` [#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#proctor-check)

Measure a PHP app against the version policy.

Usage: `proctor check [--path PATH] [--format FORMAT] [--policy POLICY] [--today TODAY] [--php-runtime PHP-RUNTIME] [--timeout TIMEOUT]`

| Option | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--path=VALUE` | Path to the application to check. | `.` |
| `--format=VALUE` | Output format (text, json, codequality, sarif). | `text` |
| `--policy=VALUE` | Path to the CREED-format policy file. Without it, PROCTOR checks the PROCTOR_POLICY environment variable, then the app's vendor/waynestate/creed/policy/policy.json, then its own bundled copy. In CI this option is refused unless PROCTOR_ALLOW_OVERRIDES=1. |  |
| `--today=VALUE` | Override today's date (YYYY-MM-DD). In CI this option is refused unless PROCTOR_ALLOW_OVERRIDES=1. |  |
| `--php-runtime=VALUE` | The PHP version that will serve the app (X.Y.Z), for the unpatched check. |  |
| `--timeout=VALUE` | Maximum seconds for composer audit before it is killed. | `300` |
| `--silent` | Do not output any message |  |

#### `proctor gate` [#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#proctor-gate)

Decide go or no-go for a deploy: the deploy-time checks, ratcheted against a baseline.

Usage: `proctor gate [--path PATH] [--format FORMAT] [--baseline BASELINE] [--record RECORD] [--policy POLICY] [--today TODAY] [--php-runtime PHP-RUNTIME] [--timeout TIMEOUT]`

| Option | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--path=VALUE` | Path to the application to deploy. | `.` |
| `--format=VALUE` | Output format (text, json). | `text` |
| `--baseline=VALUE` | What the running deployment already fails: a PROCTOR JSON report (the file --record writes) or the running source directory. Without it every failure blocks, as for a first deploy. |  |
| `--record=VALUE` | Also write the JSON verdict to this file (its folder is created), whatever --format says. A later run can read it with --baseline. |  |
| `--policy=VALUE` | Path to the CREED-format policy file. Without it, PROCTOR checks the PROCTOR_POLICY environment variable, then the app's vendor/waynestate/creed/policy/policy.json, then its own bundled copy. In CI this option is refused unless PROCTOR_ALLOW_OVERRIDES=1. |  |
| `--today=VALUE` | Override today's date (YYYY-MM-DD). In CI this option is refused unless PROCTOR_ALLOW_OVERRIDES=1. |  |
| `--php-runtime=VALUE` | The PHP version that will serve the app (X.Y.Z), for the unpatched check. |  |
| `--timeout=VALUE` | Maximum seconds for composer audit before it is killed. | `60` |
| `--silent` | Do not output any message |  |

#### Options every command accepts[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#options-every-command-accepts)

| Option | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-h`, `--help` | Display help for the given command. When no command is given display help for the list command |  |
| `-q`, `--quiet` | Only errors are displayed. All other output is suppressed |  |
| \`-v | -vv | -vvv`, `--verbose\` |
| `-V`, `--version` | Display this application version |  |
| `--ansi` | Force (or disable --no-ansi) ANSI output |  |
| `--no-ansi` | Negate the "--ansi" option |  |
| `-n`, `--no-interaction` | Do not ask any interactive question |  |

### Examples[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#examples)

Run the check against an application:

```
vendor/bin/proctor check [--path=.] [--format=text|json|codequality|sarif] [--policy=<file>] [--today=YYYY-MM-DD] [--php-runtime=X.Y.Z] [--timeout=300]
```

- `--path`: path to the application to check (default `.`).
- `--format`: output format: `text` (default), `json`, `codequality`, or `sarif`.
- `--policy`: path to the CREED-format policy file. Optional: without it, PROCTOR resolves the policy from the `PROCTOR_POLICY` environment variable, then the app's `vendor/waynestate/creed/policy/policy.json`, then the copy bundled with PROCTOR (see [Policy](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/policy.html)). In CI this option is refused unless a trusted job sets `PROCTOR_ALLOW_OVERRIDES=1`.
- `--today`: override today's date (YYYY-MM-DD) so runs are deterministic. In CI this option is refused unless a trusted job sets `PROCTOR_ALLOW_OVERRIDES=1`.
- `--php-runtime`: the PHP version that will serve the app (X.Y.Z), used by the `unpatched` check. CI should pass the deploy image's PHP, not the runner's.
- `--timeout`: seconds `composer audit` may run before it is killed (default 300). `proctor gate` defaults to 60.

Ask for a go or no-go before a deploy, against the verdict recorded last time:

```
vendor/bin/proctor gate --baseline=storage/proctor-gate.json --record=storage/proctor-gate.json
```

- `--baseline`: what the running deployment already fails: a PROCTOR JSON report or the running source directory. Without it every failure blocks, as for a first deploy.
- `--record`: also write the JSON verdict to this file, for the deploy log and the next run's `--baseline`.

The gate runs eight deploy-time checks and exits 0 (go), 1 (no-go) or 2 (could not decide); see [Deploy gate](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/deploy-gate.html).

## Configuration[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html#configuration)

This page lists every setting PROCTOR reads: the policy file and how it is found, the `extra.proctor` keys in composer.json, and the `policy-overrides.json` file an app can carry next to it. The environment table is generated from the source, so it stays in step with the code. The proctor keeps the answer sheet sealed; these are the only dials it has. If a run trips or fails, go to [Troubleshooting](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html).

| Variable | Meaning | Default | Read in |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PROCTOR_ALLOW_OVERRIDES | Set to exactly 1 by a trusted job (a protected or group-level CI variable, never the app's .gitlab-ci.yml) to allow --policy and --today in CI | none | src/Policy/CiGuard.php |
| PROCTOR_POLICY | Path to a CREED-format policy file; tried before the app's vendor copy and the bundled copy when --policy is absent | none | src/Policy/PolicyResolver.php |

Warning

None of the settings on this page take a secret. PROCTOR reads paths, dates and flags; it never asks for a token, password or key. The one nearby place credentials leak is a package source URL: a deploy token in the userinfo of a composer.json repository URL or a composer.lock source/dist URL, a `private_token`, `access_token`, `token` or `password` query parameter, or a `.npmrc` line that sets `_authToken`, `_auth` or `_password` to a literal value. The `repo-url-credentials` check warns when it sees one (the secret is masked as `***` in the message), and the fix is moving the token to `auth.json`, which is gitignored, or a CI variable, and using one registry URL without credentials.

### The policy file[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html#the-policy-file)

`--policy` takes a CREED-format policy file: schema_version 1, component versions with released, active_until and security_until dates, and rules (audit_severity_threshold, banned_constraints, eol_grace_days).

Without `--policy`, PROCTOR resolves the policy in this order (first match wins):

1. the `PROCTOR_POLICY` environment variable, naming a policy file;
2. `<app>/vendor/waynestate/creed/policy/policy.json`, when it exists and is at least as fresh as the bundled copy (same or newer `refreshed_on`);
3. the policy bundled with PROCTOR (`src/Creed/policy.json`).

An app that installs CREED gets its policy automatically:

```
composer require waynestate/creed --dev
```

A vendor copy that cannot be read or parsed is skipped with a note on stderr and the run continues with the next source; a vendor copy older than the bundled one is skipped the same way. An explicit source (`--policy` or `PROCTOR_POLICY`) that points at a missing or invalid file is still an error (exit 2).

Every report names the policy it used: origin (`option`, `env`, `vendor` or `bundled`), path, `refreshed_on` and the age in days. The `policy-age` check warns when the policy is more than 60 days old, or when a non-bundled policy has no `refreshed_on` date, so a stopped CREED refresh is visible instead of silent.

PROCTOR carries a generated copy of the CREED reader under `src/Creed/` (namespace `Waynestate\Proctor\Creed`), so it never depends on the CREED package at runtime. `composer creed-copy:check` verifies the copy against the CREED checkout named by `CREED_PATH` (default `../creed`); refresh it by running CREED's `bin/export.php` against `src/Creed/`.

Weekly CREED copy refresh: a scheduled GitLab job (`creed-copy-refresh`, Mondays, an hour after CREED's policy robot) re-exports the copy from CREED main, rebuilds the docs, runs `composer creed-copy:check` and `composer ci`, and pushes to main only when both pass. A red run leaves main untouched.

### extra.proctor in composer.json[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html#extra-proctor-in-composer-json)

An app sets PROCTOR-specific switches under `extra.proctor` in its own composer.json. The two keys PROCTOR reads:

| Key | Values | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `github-mirror` | `false` | Marks a private stack package that must never be on GitHub: a missing `.github/workflows/ci.yml` then gives no finding, and a present one warns (`proctor/ci-pipelines/github-private`) along with the warning-only rules. |
| `wayneui.copies` | `warn` (default), `fail` | In `fail` mode a behind committed copy of WayneUI is a failure, with a sentence naming the setting appended to its message, while findings from composer.lock and package-lock.json stay warnings. Only committed copies are affected by the setting, and an offline run never fails in either mode, because an unknown latest is always just the info skipped finding. |

PROCTOR's own composer.json sets `wayneui.copies` to `fail`: the proctor fails the stack's own exam halls.

### policy-overrides.json[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html#policy-overrides-json)

An app can carry a `policy-overrides.json` file next to its composer.json:

```json
[
    {
        "check": "lock-committed",
        "reason": "lock is generated by CI and not committed",
        "expires": "2027-01-31",
        "approved_by": "jane@example.wayne.edu"
    }
]
```

A `composer-audit` override may name the one thing it covers with two optional fields:

- `advisory` is an advisory id or CVE, matched case-insensitively against the finding's advisory id or CVE.
- `package` is a package name, with `*` matching any run of characters the way composer does, matched case-insensitively against the audited package.

When both are present, both must match the same advisory. Without either field the override covers every fail of the check, as before. The fields are only valid on `composer-audit`: on any other check, or with a value that is not a non-empty string, PROCTOR rejects the file (exit 2). A scoped override never covers a fail that carries no advisory data (such as the exit-code fail), and a scoped override that matches no failure earns the `proctor/overrides/unused` warning with its scope in the text.

An expired override fails the `overrides` check. An active override turns the matching fail findings of its check into warnings. An override never waives a failure whose state is EOL plus grace (eol_grace_expired); that failure stands (the stack's version policy decision).

PROCTOR rejects the file (exit 2) when an entry names a check that is not registered in the run, or names the `overrides` check itself: an override cannot exempt the check that polices overrides, and an entry for a check that does not exist would silently do nothing. The list of valid check ids is built from the checks PROCTOR runs, so a new check needs no change to the guard. An active override that expires within 14 days of `--today` (the expiry day counts) gets a warning finding (`proctor/overrides/expiring`) instead of lapsing without a trace, and an active override whose check raised no failure gets a warning finding (`proctor/overrides/unused`) so a stale approval is removed instead of rotting. A warning never changes the exit code.

## Exit codes[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/exit-codes.html#exit-codes)

This page lists the three exit codes `proctor check` and `proctor gate` end with and exactly when each one happens, so a pipeline can branch on the right one. The proctor hands back the mark sheet and leaves the hall; the code is the only word it says out loud. For what feeds the verdict, see [Rule ids](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/rule-ids.html) and the [checks overview](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/checks-overview.html).

### Codes[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/exit-codes.html#codes)

| Exit code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | pass (warnings allowed) |
| `1` | one or more failures |
| `2` | tool error (bad options, unreadable policy, a present but malformed or unreadable composer.json, or an overrides file that is malformed, unreadable, or names a check that is not registered or the overrides check itself) |

A missing composer.json is not a tool error: the app gets a verdict, with php-floor failing.

On a tool error every format still writes its report to stdout, next to the message on stderr: `text` prints the message as a FAIL line, `json` writes the report shape with `result` set to `error`, an `error` field carrying the message and empty findings, `codequality` lists the error as one blocker issue, and `sarif` writes a log whose single run reports an unsuccessful invocation. A pipeline can read the reason from the report instead of only from stderr.

### proctor gate[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/exit-codes.html#proctor-gate)

The deploy gate uses the same three numbers with deploy words (see [Deploy gate](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/deploy-gate.html)):

| Exit code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | go: nothing blocked (held and waived failures, warnings allowed) |
| `1` | no-go: a failure is blocked (a first deploy, a regression against the baseline, or an expired override) |
| `2` | the gate could not decide (the tool errors above, plus a missing or malformed `--baseline` or a `--record` file it could not write); a platform hook fails open on it |

On exit 2 the gate writes its verdict in the selected format: the JSON verdict with `verdict` set to `error`, or, for `text`, the verdict line, a FAIL line carrying the message, and a RESULT line.

### How a run ends[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/exit-codes.html#how-a-run-ends)

```mermaid
%%{init: {'theme':'base','themeVariables':{'fontFamily':'Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif','primaryColor':'#F4F1EA','primaryTextColor':'#1f2a33','primaryBorderColor':'#0C5449','lineColor':'#8A9A94'}}}%%
flowchart LR
  run["proctor check"] --> ok{"options and policy readable?"}
  ok -- no --> two["exit 2: the proctor tripped"]
  ok -- yes --> fails{"any FAIL?"}
  fails -- yes --> one["exit 1: resit"]
  fails -- no --> zero["exit 0: pass, warnings allowed"]
  classDef pass fill:#0C5449,stroke:#0C5449,color:#F4F1EA
  classDef fail fill:#9B1C2E,stroke:#9B1C2E,color:#F4F1EA
  classDef trip fill:#F4F1EA,stroke:#9B1C2E,color:#9B1C2E,stroke-dasharray:4 3
  class zero pass
  class one fail
  class two trip
```

### Watch it mark a paper[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/exit-codes.html#watch-it-mark-a-paper)

The answer sheet from the front page, handed over finished:

![The front page's answer sheet: five steps from 'pencils up' to 'resit, pencils down', nine bubbles filled, question 3 circled in red pen with the fix in the margin, the fail struck through and a PASS stamp.](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/marking.jpg)

## Proof[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#proof)

This page points at PROCTOR's proof runs against real Wayne State applications, and how the docs site and the test suite are built and run. To read a report once you have one, start with [Formats](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/formats.html).

### Last run[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#last-run)

| Check | Date | Commit | Result | Duration |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `composer ci` in Docker (composer:2.10.3) | 2026-11-07 | 4201f99 | pass: 334 tests, 4682 assertions; lint 93 files; static analysis clean; agent-ready 25 files; docs 20 pages; 0 advisories | 8 min 12 s |

To refresh this table, rerun the checks described on this page on the current commit and replace the rows with the new output. Not run here: the proof runs against real Wayne State applications, which live on a private site behind an employee sign-in.

### Proof runs[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#proof-runs)

Proof runs against real Wayne State applications are on a private site, [proof.apps.wayne.edu/proctor](https://proof.apps.wayne.edu/proctor/), behind a Wayne State employee sign-in.

### Docs[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#docs)

The documentation lives at [proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/) and is built from `docs/` by Squire's docs builder:

```
composer docs
```

renders the pages into `site/docs/` and fills the generated command and environment reference from the CLI and the source. The pages are committed, so the site stays static. Check without writing:

```
composer docs:check
```

which runs as part of `composer ci`.

### Running the tests in Docker[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#running-the-tests-in-docker)

Maintainers: how to build, test and release this project, and where its data comes from, is in [MAINTAINING.md](https://github.com/waynestate/proctor/blob/main/MAINTAINING.md).

No PHP is needed on the host:

```
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -v stack-composer-cache:/tmp/cache -w /app -e COMPOSER_PROCESS_TIMEOUT=0 composer:2.10.3 sh -c "composer install -q --no-progress && composer ci"
```

The `stack-composer-cache` volume keeps Composer's downloads between runs; Docker creates it the first time.

The plain php images lack git and composer, so 22 tests fail there; the composer image above carries both tools.

Strongly recommended: a git.wayne.edu instance runner.

## Rule ids[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/rule-ids.html#rule-ids)

Every finding carries a stable, namespaced rule id: `proctor/<check-id>` for a check's default finding, `proctor/<check-id>/<rule>` for a named rule. The id is the finding's identity in the machine formats: `rule_id` in `json`, `ruleId` in `sarif`, and `check_name` in `codequality`. A rule keeps the same id across runs and across formats even when its message changes. The table below is the full set, grouped by check.

### Rule ids by check[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/rule-ids.html#rule-ids-by-check)

| Check | Rule id |
| --- | --- |
| `php-floor` | `proctor/php-floor` |
| `unpatched` | `proctor/unpatched` |
| `laravel-eol` | `proctor/laravel-eol` |
| `laravel-php` | `proctor/laravel-php` |
| `node-eol` | `proctor/node-eol` |
| `node-eol` | `proctor/node-eol/engines` |
| `node-eol` | `proctor/node-eol/odd-major` |
| `lock-committed` | `proctor/lock-committed` |
| `lock-committed` | `proctor/lock-committed/out-of-sync` |
| `destructive-deploy` | `proctor/destructive-deploy` |
| `crlf-deploy-script` | `proctor/crlf-deploy-script` |
| `overrides` | `proctor/overrides` |
| `overrides` | `proctor/overrides/expiring` |
| `overrides` | `proctor/overrides/unused` |
| `unbounded-constraints` | `proctor/unbounded-constraints` |
| `unbounded-constraints` | `proctor/unbounded-constraints/unbounded` |
| `unbounded-constraints` | `proctor/unbounded-constraints/repository` |
| `unbounded-constraints` | `proctor/unbounded-constraints/minimum-stability` |
| `unbounded-constraints` | `proctor/unbounded-constraints/insecure-url` |
| `composer-config` | `proctor/composer-config` |
| `composer-config` | `proctor/composer-config/allow-plugins-all` |
| `composer-config` | `proctor/composer-config/secure-http-off` |
| `composer-config` | `proctor/composer-config/lock-off` |
| `composer-config` | `proctor/composer-config/audit-blocking-off` |
| `composer-config` | `proctor/composer-config/policy-off` |
| `composer-config` | `proctor/composer-config/policy-malware-off` |
| `composer-config` | `proctor/composer-config/policy-advisories-off` |
| `composer-config` | `proctor/composer-config/platform-php-unset` |
| `portability` | `proctor/portability` |
| `portability` | `proctor/portability/host-path` |
| `portability` | `proctor/portability/proxy-address` |
| `portability` | `proctor/portability/local-session` |
| `portability` | `proctor/portability/htaccess-php-setting` |
| `portability` | `proctor/portability/parse-error` |
| `portability` | `proctor/portability/dynamic-call` |
| `mysql56` | `proctor/mysql56` |
| `mysql56` | `proctor/mysql56/json` |
| `mysql56` | `proctor/mysql56/generated` |

| `composer-audit` | `proctor/composer-audit/advisory` |

| `served-folder` | `proctor/served-folder/phpinfo` |

`proctor/composer-audit/skipped` is a failure, not an info finding: it fires when the composer executable is not on PATH or the app has no composer.lock, its message starts with `not audited:`, and an active `composer-audit` override downgrades it to a warning.

### Kept in step[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/rule-ids.html#kept-in-step)

`tests/RuleIdContractTest.php` keeps this table in step with the checks: a rule id that is emitted but not listed in the known set fails the suite, and the test parses the README's copy of this table, so a known rule id missing from it, or a row that names an unknown rule id, fails the suite too. The proctor stamps each id in pencil so small only the head office can read it, and it never smudges.

## Troubleshooting[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#troubleshooting)

How to work through a PROCTOR run that trips, warns or fails, starting from the exit code and ending at the fix. A proctor that trips over the desk has not marked your paper: exit 2 is the proctor's problem, exit 1 is yours, and warnings are notes in the margin.

### Read the run in order[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#read-the-run-in-order)

1. **The exit code.** `0`: pass (warnings allowed). `1`: one or more failures. `2`: tool error. A warning never changes the exit code, so a red run always has a failure behind it.
2. **The policy line.** Every report names the policy in use: origin (`option`, `env`, `vendor` or `bundled`), path, `refreshed_on` and the age in days. If the run looks wrong, check which policy answered before blaming the checks.
3. **The findings.** One line per finding in the text format, each carrying a stable rule id. The [Rule ids](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/rule-ids.html) page maps every id to its check.

### Exit 2: the proctor tripped[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#exit-2-the-proctor-tripped)

A tool error means PROCTOR could not run the checks. The causes it reports:

#### Bad options[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#bad-options)

The run named an option the command does not accept, or a value it cannot read.

- Fix: correct the option against the [Commands](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html) page.
- Check: `vendor/bin/proctor check --help` lists what the command accepts.

#### The message starts with `Refused:` [#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#the-message-starts-with-refused)

In CI (any of `CI`, `GITLAB_CI` or `GITHUB_ACTIONS` set to a value other than `0` or `false`), `--policy` and `--today` are refused (exit 2) unless the job sets `PROCTOR_ALLOW_OVERRIDES=1`: in CI the policy and the date must come from the stack, not from the app being checked, so a pipeline that could pass its own policy or date could grade itself. The message names the option or options that were given.

- Fix: drop `--policy` and let the policy resolve from the `PROCTOR_POLICY` variable (which stays allowed in CI), then the app's `vendor/waynestate/creed/policy/policy.json`, then the bundled copy; drop `--today`, or move the option to a trusted job that sets `PROCTOR_ALLOW_OVERRIDES: "1"` as a protected or group-level CI variable, never in the app's own `.gitlab-ci.yml`.
- Check: rerun in CI; the run reaches the checks when no refused option is present, or the trusted job allows them. Outside CI the same command runs unchanged.

#### The message names a policy file[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#the-message-names-a-policy-file)

An explicit source (`--policy` or `PROCTOR_POLICY`) that points at a missing or invalid file is an error (exit 2). A vendor copy that cannot be read or parsed, or that is older than the bundled one, is not an error: it is skipped with a note on stderr and the run continues with the next source.

- Fix: correct the path or the file, or drop the explicit source and let the policy resolve from the `PROCTOR_POLICY` variable, then the app's `vendor/waynestate/creed/policy/policy.json`, then the bundled copy.
- Check: rerun and read the policy line; it names the origin, path, `refreshed_on` and age of the policy that answered.

#### The message names policy-overrides.json[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#the-message-names-policy-overrides-json)

The file is rejected before any check runs when it is malformed or unreadable, when an entry names a check that is not registered in the run, or when an entry names the `overrides` check itself: an override cannot exempt the check that polices overrides, and an entry for a check that does not exist would silently do nothing.

- Fix: repair the JSON, and use a check id that PROCTOR actually runs; the list of valid ids is built from the checks PROCTOR runs, so a new check needs no change to the guard.
- Check: rerun; the file must parse and name only registered checks before any check runs.

#### composer.json is present but malformed[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#composer-json-is-present-but-malformed)

A present but malformed or unreadable composer.json is a tool error. A missing composer.json is not: the app gets a verdict, with `php-floor` failing.

- Fix: repair the JSON, or point `--path` at the application root that has one.
- Check: rerun; with a readable composer.json the run reaches the checks.

### Failures that mean what they say[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#failures-that-mean-what-they-say)

#### composer-audit fails with `not audited:` [#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#composer-audit-fails-with-not-audited)

Rule id `proctor/composer-audit/could-not-run`. The audit ran but its stdout was not parseable JSON; the message starts with `not audited:` and carries the first stderr line, because a green run that audited nothing is worse than a red one.

- Fix: read the stderr line in the message and fix what composer reported. Composer audit runs with `--no-plugins --no-interaction` and a minimal explicit environment (PATH plus the variables composer needs to start), so inherited `COMPOSER_*` switches no longer reach it.
- Check: rerun the check; only a clean audit with a clean result passes.

#### composer-audit fails with `not audited:` because composer is missing[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#composer-audit-fails-with-not-audited-because-composer-is-missing)

Rule id `proctor/composer-audit/skipped`. The message reads `not audited: composer executable not found on PATH; install Composer or record an override`: there is no composer executable on PATH, so the audit could not run at all. A skipped audit must never look like a pass.

- Fix: install Composer on the runner, or record an active `composer-audit` override in policy-overrides.json with a reason and an expiry to downgrade the fail to a warning.
- Check: rerun; once composer is found, the audit runs and is graded as usual.

#### composer-audit fails with `not audited:` because the lock is missing[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#composer-audit-fails-with-not-audited-because-the-lock-is-missing)

Rule id `proctor/composer-audit/skipped`. The message reads `not audited: no composer.lock in the app path; commit the lock or record an override`: the app path has no composer.lock, so `composer audit --locked` has nothing to audit.

- Fix: commit the lock file (`composer update --lock` regenerates it), or record an active `composer-audit` override in policy-overrides.json with a reason and an expiry to downgrade the fail to a warning.
- Check: rerun; with the lock present, the audit runs and is graded as usual.

#### composer-audit fails with no advisory listed[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#composer-audit-fails-with-no-advisory-listed)

Rule id `proctor/composer-audit/exit-code`. Since Composer 2.10 the audit exits 1 when anything failed it, so a non-zero exit whose JSON lists nothing PROCTOR can read (a malware or policy block, or an error) is itself a fail, and only a clean exit with a clean result passes.

- Fix: address what Composer blocked: the block is real, not a PROCTOR misread.
- Check: run with `--format=json` and read the finding.

#### composer-audit fails because an ignore entry has no matching override[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#composer-audit-fails-because-an-ignore-entry-has-no-matching-override)

Rule id `proctor/composer-audit/unbacked-ignore`. The message reads `ignore entry "<entry>" in composer.json has no matching override; record it in policy-overrides.json with a reason and an expiry`: the app silences an audit result in its own composer.json, and no active `composer-audit` override in policy-overrides.json backs that entry. An ignore without a dated approval never expires, so each unbacked entry fails instead of warning.

- Fix: record an active `composer-audit` override in policy-overrides.json that backs the entry: its `advisory` field equals the entry's advisory id case-insensitively, its `package` field matches the entry's package, or the override carries no scope at all (the only shape that backs an ignore-severity level). Remove the ignore entry from composer.json when the override expires.
- Check: rerun; the entry earns no `unbacked-ignore` fail, the count warning (`proctor/composer-audit/ignore-entries`) still reports it, and the backing override is not flagged `proctor/overrides/unused`.

#### lock-committed fails[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#lock-committed-fails)

`composer.lock` is missing from the app path.

- Fix: commit the lock file.
- Check: rerun; with the lock present, a `content-hash` that no longer matches composer.json warns (`proctor/lock-committed/out-of-sync`) instead of failing, so regenerate the lock when the warning appears and the warning never changes the exit code.

#### destructive-deploy fails[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#destructive-deploy-fails)

A deploy script runs an artisan command that drops or rebuilds the database (`migrate:fresh`, `migrate:refresh`, `migrate:reset`, `db:wipe`), which erases production data on every deploy. Scanned: `.sh` and `.php` files under a top-level `deployments/`, `deploy_scripts/`, `deploy/` or `scripts/` directory, the top-level `build.sh`, `release.sh` and `.gitlab-ci.yml`, and the `scripts` section of composer.json; shell comments are ignored.

- Fix: run plain `php artisan migrate --force` in the deploy.
- Check: rerun; the check passes when no scanned script drops or rebuilds the database.

#### php-floor fails and there is no composer.json[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#php-floor-fails-and-there-is-no-composer-json)

Intended behavior: a missing composer.json is not a tool error, so the app gets a verdict, with `php-floor` failing.

- Fix: point `--path` at the application root that carries the composer.json.
- Check: rerun against the right path.

### Warnings that deserve a look[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#warnings-that-deserve-a-look)

#### proctor/policy-age[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#proctor-policy-age)

The policy in use is more than 60 days old (its `refreshed_on` date is more than 60 days before `--today`), or a non-bundled policy has no `refreshed_on` date. It exists so a stopped CREED refresh robot is visible instead of silent.

- Fix: refresh the policy: `composer update waynestate/creed` for the vendor copy, or point `--policy` or `PROCTOR_POLICY` at a current file. Warning only: an old policy never fails a run, and the bundled policy may omit the date.

#### proctor/overrides/expiring and proctor/overrides/unused[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#proctor-overrides-expiring-and-proctor-overrides-unused)

An active entry in policy-overrides.json that expires within 14 days of `--today` (the expiry day counts) warns `expiring`, so an approval that is about to lapse is visible instead of silent. An active entry that matches no failure warns `unused`, so a stale approval is removed instead of rotting.

- Fix: renew the entry with a new `expires` date and approver, or delete it. A warning never changes the exit code; an expired entry, however, fails the `overrides` check.

#### proctor/repo-url-credentials[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#proctor-repo-url-credentials)

A credential is written into a package source URL: a deploy token in the userinfo of a composer.json repository URL or a composer.lock source/dist URL, a bare token user of 20+ characters, a `private_token`, `access_token`, `token` or `password` query parameter, or a `.npmrc` line that sets `_authToken`, `_auth` or `_password` to a literal value (`${SOME_VAR}` is fine). The secret is masked as `***` in the message, so the report itself is safe to hand back.

- Fix: move the token to `auth.json`, which is gitignored, or a CI variable, and use one registry URL without credentials.
- Check: rerun; the warning clears when no scanned URL carries a literal credential.

#### proctor/ci-pipelines/composer-audit-off[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#proctor-ci-pipelines-composer-audit-off)

The pipeline environment switches Composer's audit or blocking policy off: `COMPOSER_NO_AUDIT` or `COMPOSER_NO_BLOCKING` set to anything but an empty string, `0` or `false`, or `COMPOSER_AUDIT_ABANDONED` set to `ignore`, in the GitLab top-level or job `variables:` (a scalar or a map with a `value` key) or the GitHub top-level, job or step `env:`.

- Fix: remove the switch from the pipeline environment. A warning, never a fail, for stack packages and other projects alike.

#### A dev-dependency advisory is only a warning[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#a-dev-dependency-advisory-is-only-a-warning)

An advisory whose package composer.lock lists only in `packages-dev` is a warning at any severity, with the message ending in ` [dev dependency]`. It still needs fixing: dev tools run in CI, and a vulnerable test runner is a real attack surface even though it is not in the deployed image.

- Fix: update the dev dependency the way you would any other (`composer update vendor/package --with-dependencies`), or record a dated `composer-audit` override in policy-overrides.json if the upgrade is blocked.
- Check: open `composer.lock` and look for the package name under `packages-dev`; if it also appears under `packages`, it counts as runtime and the advisory fails at or above the threshold as usual.

#### portability warnings from bootstrap/cache/[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#portability-warnings-from-bootstrap-cache)

In a Laravel app (an `artisan` file at the project root) the top-level `bootstrap/cache/` is skipped, so the files `php artisan optimize` writes there (`config.php`, `routes-v7.php`, `services.php`, `packages.php`, `events.php`) do not raise warnings and hide real findings. If you still see them, the app has no `artisan` at the root: a raw-PHP app that keeps its own `bootstrap/cache/` folder is scanned as before.

- Fix: put `artisan` at the project root, or move the generated output out of the scanned directories.
- Check: rerun; the generated cache files stop appearing once the app is recognized as Laravel.

### Results that follow the environment[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#results-that-follow-the-environment)

#### unpatched disagrees with the deploy[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#unpatched-disagrees-with-the-deploy)

`--php-runtime` is the PHP version that will serve the app (X.Y.Z), used by the `unpatched` check. CI should pass the deploy image's PHP, not the runner's.

- Fix: pass `--php-runtime` matching the deploy image in CI.
- Check: rerun with the flag; the runtime finding follows the version you pass.

#### The same app gives different results on different days[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#the-same-app-gives-different-results-on-different-days)

`--today` overrides today's date (YYYY-MM-DD) so runs are deterministic; `policy-age` and the overrides expiring window both compare against it.

- Fix: pin `--today` in CI so a policy refresh or an override renewal does not change the verdict mid-week.
- Check: rerun twice with the same `--today`; the findings match.

#### An offline run reports proctor/wayneui-outdated/skipped[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#an-offline-run-reports-proctor-wayneui-outdated-skipped)

When the lookup cannot run (no composer on PATH, offline, or no parsable versions) the check reports one info finding with the skipped marker and nothing else, so an offline run never breaks.

- No fix needed: the version comparison resumes when the release list can be read, and an offline run never fails in either mode, because an unknown latest is always just the info skipped finding.

### You are on an older PROCTOR[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#you-are-on-an-older-proctor)

Some symptoms were bugs, fixed in a release. Check your version first:

```
composer show waynestate/proctor
```

- Exit 255 with `Allowed memory size exhausted` while scanning a large app: fixed in 0.2.4. Each file's syntax tree is dropped before the next file is parsed, and `bin/proctor` raises a memory limit below 512M to 512M (a higher limit or -1 is left alone).
- Every advisory named `unknown`: fixed in 0.2.8. PROCTOR reads Composer's real audit JSON, and each finding reads `<package> <version>: <CVE or advisory id> <title> (<severity>)`.
- The app's ignore list matched nothing: fixed in 0.2.8. `config.policy.advisories.ignore-id`, `config.policy.advisories.ignore` (by package) and the legacy `config.audit.ignore` are read in both their list and map shapes, matching any of the advisory's ids.
- A `?` in the text report is not corruption: since 0.3.1, terminal control characters in app-supplied strings (finding messages, override reasons and approvers) print as a visible `?`. Clean the string at the source.

### Related[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#related)

## Upgrading[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#upgrading)

PROCTOR is the invigilator, so upgrading it is a seat change, not a new exam: same hall, fresher pen. This page tells you how to move an app from one PROCTOR release to the next and which changes affect your runs. Start with the release that has a break, then work down to the additive ones.

### 0.8.0[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-8-0)

Released 2026-11-08. This is a pre-1.0 minor: consumers that pin `^0.7` stay on 0.7.x until they move their constraint to `^0.8`. Most of what is new is additive or a warning (the `mysql-eol` check, the `X-Sesame-Assertion` read in `raw-identity-header`, the ADVISOR module, release tags accepted by `preflight-pinned`), but one change can turn a passing run into a failing one.

#### Breaking[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#breaking)

- `crlf-deploy-script` fails an app whose deploy script has Windows line endings (CRLF): the top-level `build.sh` and `release.sh`, and any `.sh` under `deployments/`, `deploy_scripts/`, `deploy/` or `scripts/`. Bash on Linux reads the carriage return as part of each command, so such a script was already broken on the host; PROCTOR now says so before the deploy does. Convert the file to LF and add `*.sh text eol=lf` to `.gitattributes`.

#### Changed[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#changed)

- `mysql-eol` is new and warns, never fails, while Citadel's shared database server is MySQL 5.6 (D-008, D-053). It grades the MySQL or MariaDB version named in a root compose file and in `SQUIRE_MYSQL_IMAGE` in `.env.example` or `.env.squire.example`: a security-only line warns with the days left, an end-of-life line warns as `eol_grace_expired` and says to move to MySQL 8.4 or later, and a floating major tag such as `mysql:8` warns until you pin a major.minor. It turns into a fail once Citadel offers a supported MySQL, so treat these warnings as the to-do list for that day.
- `raw-identity-header` also warns on a direct read of `X-Sesame-Assertion`, the signed assertion Drawbridge sends. Only SESAME's gateway driver should read it; take the user from SESAME instead.
- `preflight-pinned` accepts a Preflight component pinned to a full release tag such as `@0.3.0` as well as a commit SHA (D-054), so a tag pin no longer warns. A branch, `~latest` or a partial version such as `@0.3` still warns.

#### Deprecated[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#deprecated)

- None recorded so far.

#### Steps[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#steps)

1. Move the PROCTOR constraint in your composer.json from `^0.7` to `^0.8`, then apply it with `composer require waynestate/proctor --dev`.
2. Re-run the check in CI and read any `crlf-deploy-script` finding first, then the `mysql-eol` warnings:
   ```bash
   vendor/bin/proctor check
   ```

#### How to verify[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#how-to-verify)

- Run `vendor/bin/proctor check --format=json` and confirm the `version` field reads `0.8.0`.

### 0.7.0[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-7-0)

Released 2026-11-07. This is a pre-1.0 minor: consumers that pin `^0.6` stay on 0.6.x until they move their constraint to `^0.7`. Most of what is new is additive (`proctor gate`, the deploy gate, and the `raw-identity-header`, `env-outside-config`, `app-key`, `served-folder`, `laravel-php` and `laravel-eol` checks), but one change can turn a passing run into a failing one.

#### Breaking[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#breaking-1)

- `node-eol` fails an app that pins an end-of-life Node line (Node 20 or older under the bundled policy, as of 2026-04-30). Node 20 is past the grace window, so it fails as `eol_grace_expired`, which no override softens: move to Node 22 or 24.

#### Deprecated[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#deprecated-1)

- None recorded so far.

#### Steps[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#steps-1)

1. Move the PROCTOR constraint in your composer.json from `^0.6` to `^0.7`, then apply it with `composer require waynestate/proctor --dev`.
2. Re-run the check in CI and read any `node-eol` finding first:
   ```bash
   vendor/bin/proctor check
   ```

#### How to verify[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#how-to-verify-1)

- Run `vendor/bin/proctor check --format=json` and confirm the `version` field reads `0.7.0`.

### 0.6.0[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-6-0)

Released 2026-11-05. This is a pre-1.0 minor: consumers that pin `^0.5` stay on 0.5.x until they move their constraint to `^0.6`. Most of what is new is additive, but three changes can turn a passing run into a failing one.

#### Breaking[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#breaking-2)

- `composer-audit` fails when the composer executable is not on PATH or the app has no composer.lock (rule id `proctor/composer-audit/skipped`, message starting with `not audited:`). An app whose audit could not run used to pass with an info line; it now exits non-zero until Composer is installed, the lock is committed, or an active `composer-audit` override with a reason and an expiry downgrades the fail to a warning.
- `composer-audit` fails each ignore entry in composer.json that no active `composer-audit` override backs (rule id `proctor/composer-audit/unbacked-ignore`). An app that silences audit results in its own composer.json used to earn only a count warning; it now exits non-zero until every entry is backed by an active override whose `advisory` field names the entry's advisory id, whose `package` field matches the entry's package, or that carries no scope at all. Steps: record one such entry per unbacked ignore in policy-overrides.json with a reason and an expiry, keep the composer.json ignore until the override expires, then remove the ignore entry.
- **Refused `--policy` and `--today` in CI.** In CI (any of `CI`, `GITLAB_CI` or `GITHUB_ACTIONS` set to a value other than `0` or `false`), `proctor check` now refuses `--policy` and `--today` with a tool error (exit 2) unless the job sets `PROCTOR_ALLOW_OVERRIDES=1`. In CI the policy and the date must come from the stack, not from the app being checked: a pipeline that could pass its own policy or date could grade itself. Pipelines that pass these options must either set `PROCTOR_ALLOW_OVERRIDES: "1"` as a variable of a trusted job (a protected or group-level CI variable, never the app's own `.gitlab-ci.yml`) or drop the option: name the policy with the `PROCTOR_POLICY` environment variable instead of `--policy` (it stays allowed in CI), and drop `--today` or let the trusted job allow it. Outside CI nothing changes.

#### Changed[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#changed-1)

- An app that failed only because of a dev-only advisory now warns instead. An advisory on a package that composer.lock lists only in `packages-dev` is a warning at any severity, with the message ending in ` [dev dependency]`; a name in both lists counts as runtime and still fails at or above the threshold. No action is required unless you want the dev dependency updated, because dev tools run in CI.

#### Deprecated[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#deprecated-2)

- None recorded so far.

#### Steps[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#steps-2)

1. Move the PROCTOR constraint in your composer.json from `^0.5` to `^0.6`, then apply it with `composer require waynestate/proctor --dev`.
2. Re-run the check in CI and read any `Refused:` message first:
   ```bash
   vendor/bin/proctor check
   ```
3. For each refused option, either set `PROCTOR_ALLOW_OVERRIDES` to `1` on the trusted job (GitLab: group Settings, CI/CD, Variables, scope Protected), or drop the option and name the policy with `PROCTOR_POLICY`.
4. Make sure Composer and composer.lock are present where the check runs, or record a composer-audit override.

#### How to verify[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#how-to-verify-2)

- Run `vendor/bin/proctor check --format=json` and confirm the `version` field reads `0.6.0`.
- Run `vendor/bin/proctor check` in CI: the run reaches the checks when no refused option is present, or the trusted job sets `PROCTOR_ALLOW_OVERRIDES=1`.
- Confirm the refusal names only the option or options that were given (`Refused: --policy is not accepted in CI, ...`, `Refused: --today is not accepted in CI, ...`, or both named together).

### 0.5.0[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-5-0)

Released 2026-11-03. This is a pre-1.0 minor: consumers that pin `^0.4` stay on 0.4.x until they move their constraint to `^0.5`. Most of what is new warns and never fails, but one check can now turn a passing run into a failing one.

#### Breaking[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#breaking-3)

- `composer-audit` fails when `composer audit` runs but its output is not parseable JSON (rule id `proctor/composer-audit/could-not-run`, message starting `not audited:`). A run that audited nothing used to pass quietly; it now exits non-zero, so an app whose audit cannot run will go red until the audit is fixed.
- Consumers that pin `^0.4` stay on 0.4.x until they move their constraint to `^0.5`.

#### Deprecated[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#deprecated-3)

- None recorded for this release.

#### Steps[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#steps-3)

1. Move the PROCTOR constraint in your composer.json from `^0.4` to `^0.5`.
2. Apply it with the install command from the README:
   ```bash
   composer require waynestate/proctor --dev
   ```
3. Re-run the check, and read any `not audited:` failure first:
   ```bash
   vendor/bin/proctor check
   ```

#### How to verify[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#how-to-verify-3)

- Run `vendor/bin/proctor check --format=json` and confirm the `version` field reads `0.5.0`.
- Confirm the new warnings appear where they apply. They warn and never fail:
  - `composer-config` warns when composer.json switches Composer's dependency policy off (`proctor/composer-config/policy-off`, `policy-malware-off`, `policy-advisories-off`).
  - `ci-pipelines` warns when the pipeline environment switches Composer's audit or blocking policy off (`proctor/ci-pipelines/composer-audit-off`).
  - `composer-audit` also counts ignore entries under `config.policy` (`proctor/composer-audit/ignore-entries`), and a policy override may name one advisory or package.

### 0.4.0[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-4-0)

Released 2026-11-03. This is a pre-1.0 minor: consumers that pin `^0.3` stay on 0.3.x until they move their constraint to `^0.4`. The new checks warn and never fail.

#### Breaking[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#breaking-4)

- Consumers that pin `^0.3` stay on 0.3.x until they move their constraint to `^0.4`. That constraint move is the only break in this release.

#### Deprecated[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#deprecated-4)

- None recorded for this release.

#### Steps[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#steps-4)

1. Move the PROCTOR constraint in your composer.json from `^0.3` to `^0.4`.
2. Apply it with the install command from the README:
   ```bash
   composer require waynestate/proctor --dev
   ```
3. Re-run the check so the new checks take part:
   ```bash
   vendor/bin/proctor check
   ```

#### How to verify[#](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#how-to-verify-4)

- Run `vendor/bin/proctor check --format=json` and confirm the `version` field reads `0.4.0`.
- Confirm the checks added in this release appear in the report. They warn and never fail, so the exit code of a run that passed before should not change:
  - `composer-audit` reports the count of audit ignore entries (`proctor/composer-audit/ignore-entries`).
  - `overrides` warns when an active entry matches no failure (`proctor/overrides/unused`).
  - `unbounded-constraints` warns on a repository URL that is plain http (`proctor/unbounded-constraints/insecure-url`) and on a `minimum-stability` below stable (`proctor/unbounded-constraints/minimum-stability`).
  - `preflight-pinned` warns when a Preflight component is included at a ref that is not a commit SHA, or when an app overrides the script of an included Preflight job.
  - `lock-committed` warns when the composer.lock content-hash differs from composer.json.

The other released versions (0.1.0 through 0.3.1) record no break in the changelog; they add checks and fixes, and the upgrade command is the same for every move:

```bash
composer require waynestate/proctor --dev
```
